newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-KREKENAVOS EXPECTS 3-4 MLN LITAS PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-KREKENAVOS EXPECTS 3-4 MLN LITAS PROFIT.

text.p: Lithuanian food processor Krekenavos said on Wednesday that it expected a profit of three to four million litas this year after netting only 151,000 litas in 1996.
"If there are no unexpected developments, we plan a three to four million litas net profit in 1997," the company's general director Alfredas Stekeliunas told Reuters by telephone.
The company, located near the northern city of Panevezhys, is listed on the Vilnius bourse's A group.
The company's net profit in 1996 fell to 151,000 litas from 1.2 million litas the year before.
Stekeliunas would not comment on why the company's profits dropped in 1996, but said that it had invested heavily in a new cattle grain factory last year.
"We invested 3.3 million German marks in our cattle grain factory, which is the most modern of its kind in Lithuania," he said.
"We plan to produce 60,000 tonnes of cattle grain per year and this should bring us an annual revenue of 40 million litas," he said.
"We also invested 400,000 litas so far this year in upgrading our meat processing lines and hope that this side of our operations will bring in annual revenue of 50 million litas," he added.
The company's total turnover last year was almost 38 million litas, according to a statement of unaudited results.
He also said that the company acquired a canned food factory in the town of Kedainiai in 1996 which is in the process of being upgraded.
Its operations should begin in the fall of this year, he said.
Stekeliunas said that the vast majority of the firm's 34 million litas worth of share capital was in private hands and it had no inentions to boost it this year.
